sense: a stage in a process or a life

evidence: Ov. Met. 4.59: nōtitiam prīmōsque gradūs vīcīnia fēcit
Cic. Att. 7.23.2: hunc gradum meī reditūs esse, that this was a step towards my return (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 384: stage of life, aetātis gradus
terms.comment: A step, and so a stage on the way to something: the first stages of a love, a step towards a return. It has many other senses: a pace, a stance, a stair or rung, a degree of kinship or rank (Lewis & Short); see step, rung.

terms.gloss: a time of life, an age
evidence: Cic. Sen. 76: cōnstāns aetās, quae media dīcitur (Lewis & Short, s.v. cōnstāns)
terms.comment: For the phases of a life (childhood, youth, the settled middle years, old age). It is also a lifetime, a generation, an era (see generation).

evidence: M-O s.v. stage (a period within a process or course of development)
terms.comment: Classically a stade (a measure of length) or a race-course; Morgan–Owens finds the sense “stage” in nineteenth-century medical Latin (the stages of a disease) and marks it modern.

phrases.latin: nōtitiam prīmōsque gradūs vīcīnia fēcit: tempore crēvit amor
phrases.english: living next door gave them their acquaintance and the first steps; with time love grew

sources: Lewis & Short: gradus · Lewis & Short: aetas · Lewis & Short: stadium
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. stage. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 384.
